# BEAR.QueryRepository

> Distributed caching framework for BEAR.Sunday applications using CQRS pattern

BEAR.QueryRepository separates query (read) and command (write) operations to optimize caching and performance.

## Reference

For conceptual documentation (Donut Cache, Cache Dependencies, CQRS pattern, etc.),
see the BEAR.Sunday documentation: https://bearsunday.github.io/llms-full.txt

## Features

- Event-driven cache invalidation
- Automatic dependency resolution between cached resources
- Donut caching (`#[CacheableResponse]`/`#[DonutCache]`: a stored page template whose embedded holes are rendered per request or on events)
- CDN integration (Fastly, Akamai)
- ETag support for conditional requests
- Redis and Memcached support

## Installation

```bash
composer require bear/query-repository
```

## Attributes

### #[Cacheable]

Class attribute. Stores the `onGet()` response; a write to the resource refreshes it. Without a lifetime the entry lives until a write invalidates it.

```php
use BEAR\RepositoryModule\Annotation\Cacheable;

#[Cacheable]                   // no lifetime (default expiry: 'never'): kept until a write invalidates it, client gets max-age=0
#[Cacheable(expiry: 'short')]  // 60 seconds
#[Cacheable(expiry: 'medium')] // 1 hour
#[Cacheable(expiry: 'long')]   // 1 day
#[Cacheable(expirySecond: 300)] // Custom TTL
#[Cacheable(expiryAt: 'expiry_at')] // Until the time in $body['expiry_at']
```

Parameters:
- `expiry`: 'short' | 'medium' | 'long' | 'never' (default). The store keeps a `never` entry under the `never` preset (31536000 seconds by default); the presets come from the `Expiry` binding
- `expirySecond`: Custom TTL in seconds
- `expiryAt`: Body key holding the expiry time as a `strtotime()` string; a missing key throws `ExpireAtKeyNotExists`. Precedence: `expiryAt`, then `expirySecond`, then `expiry`
- `type`: 'value' (body only) | 'view' (body + rendered view)

### #[HttpCache]

Controls HTTP Cache-Control headers.

```php
use BEAR\RepositoryModule\Annotation\HttpCache;

#[HttpCache(maxAge: 60, sMaxAge: 600)]
#[HttpCache(isPrivate: true, maxAge: 300)]
#[HttpCache(noCache: true, mustRevalidate: true)]
```

Parameters:
- `isPrivate`: Private vs public cache
- `noCache`: Force revalidation
- `noStore`: Disable storage
- `mustRevalidate`: Require revalidation when stale
- `maxAge`: Client cache lifetime (seconds)
- `sMaxAge`: Shared cache (CDN) lifetime (seconds)
- `etag`: Body keys whose string values make the ETag instead of the whole representation (partial ETag)

### #[NoHttpCache]

Shorthand for disabling HTTP caching.

```php
use BEAR\RepositoryModule\Annotation\NoHttpCache;

#[NoHttpCache]  // Outputs: private, no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate
```

On a resource that declares `#[HttpCache]` or `#[NoHttpCache]`, this package sets the `Cache-Control` of a 200 response from the attribute and replaces one the resource or its caller sets. Declare the directives instead of setting the header.

A resource stored by `#[Cacheable]`, `#[CacheableResponse]` or `#[DonutCache]` must not declare `isPrivate`, `noStore` or `#[NoHttpCache]`: this package is a shared cache, so storing its response throws `UnstorableDeclaration` and stores nothing. When a write rebuilds its cache, the write has already run when the exception is thrown.

### #[Refresh]

After a write that answers below 400, purges the URI and reads it again with a GET, which stores what any GET of that resource stores. The URI template expands from the write's body, then its query.

```php
use BEAR\RepositoryModule\Annotation\Refresh;

#[Refresh(uri: 'app://self/user')]
#[Refresh(uri: 'app://self/user/{id}')]  // URI template
public function onPut(int $id): static { ... }
```

### #[Purge]

After a write that answers below 400, purges the URI. The template expands as for `#[Refresh]`.

```php
use BEAR\RepositoryModule\Annotation\Purge;

#[Purge(uri: 'app://self/user/{id}')]
public function onDelete(int $id): static { ... }
```

A `#[Refresh]`/`#[Purge]` template must carry every required `onGet()` parameter of the resource it names, under its own name or its snake_case form (`user_id` for `$userId`). Otherwise the write throws `TemplateLacksRequiredParameter` before it runs.

A list given to an exploded query variable (`?id={ids*}`, `{?id*}`) names one URI per element, and several lists name every combination; an empty list names none. In `{?id*}` the keys come from the value, so the required-parameter check does not apply to it.

```php
#[Purge(uri: 'app://self/tag?id={ids*}')]
public function onPost(array $ids): static { ... }  // ids: [1, 2] purges tag?id=1 and tag?id=2
```

### Purging query variants

A purge also reaches the query variants of the URI it names that differ from it only in default-valued `onGet()` parameters or in queries `onGet()` does not declare. Each cache entry also carries a group tag: its URI with every default-valued `onGet()` parameter, and any query `onGet()` does not declare, dropped. `purge()`, `#[Purge]` and `#[Refresh]` invalidate the named URI's own tag and its group tag, so purging `app://self/articles` drops `?page=2`. A variant that differs in a required parameter is a separate group. A parent that embeds a variant carries the variant's group tag as well and is dropped with it.

- A write method of a `#[Cacheable]` or `#[CacheableResponse]` resource, and one marked `#[RefreshCache]` or `#[CacheableResponse]`, purges its own URI with default-valued parameters dropped, so it reaches every variant even when the write request supplies one. A write method of any other resource that has an `onGet()`, `#[DonutCache]` included, purges its own URI the same way, as `#[Purge]` of itself would, with no GET afterwards since nothing stores it. Its own URI and the URIs its `#[Purge]`/`#[Refresh]` name are purged once each, compared as the URI string with its query, so its own URI and a `#[Purge]` of the same URI are one purge; then each `#[Refresh]` target is read again. A write whose query lacks a parameter its `onGet()` requires (a creating POST has no id yet) does not purge its own URI; a parameter `#[ResourceParam]` binds is not required, as it is not in the URI a GET is stored under. On a resource with no cache attribute it logs `purge_skipped` and its `#[Purge]`/`#[Refresh]` still run. On a `#[Cacheable]` or `#[CacheableResponse]` resource, or a method marked `#[RefreshCache]` or `#[CacheableResponse]`, a POST logs `cache_error` (`UnmatchedQuery`) and its `#[Purge]`/`#[Refresh]` still run, while a PUT, PATCH or DELETE throws `UnmatchedQuery` after the write has run, and its `#[Purge]`/`#[Refresh]` do not. A resource without `onGet()` has no key and purges nothing of its own.
- A purge URI that spells out a default-valued parameter (`app://self/articles?page=1`) is not coarsened and reaches only that URI's entries.
- A required key keeps the spelling the request used. A purge reaches a GET's entries only when it spells each required key the same way: `?user_id=1` reaches `?user_id=1&page=2`, `?userId=1` does not. The automatic purge after a write purges two spellings: every required key as the parameter name (`userId`), and every one in snake_case (`user_id`). A GET that mixes the two across its required keys (`?userId=1&post_id=2`) is not reached.
- A non-200 GET response invalidates only its own URI's tag; cached variants stay.

### #[DependsOn]

Declares a dependency that only the data reveals when it is read: a list depends on `article?id=1` and `article?id=2` because the rows it read name them. It tags the stored resource with each URI the template expands to, so a write to that URI invalidates it and every page that embeds it, without an `#[Embed]` per row.

```php
use BEAR\RepositoryModule\Annotation\DependsOn;

#[Cacheable]
class ArticleList extends ResourceObject
{
    #[DependsOn(uri: 'app://self/article?id={id}', key: 'articles')]
    public function onGet(): static
    {
        $this->body['articles'] = $this->query->list(); // [['id' => 1, 'title' => 'aaa'], ['id' => 2, 'title' => 'bbb']]

        return $this;
    }
}
```

The list is tagged with `app://self/article?id=1` and `?id=2`, and a write to either invalidates it.

- `key` names the rows in the body `onGet()` returns. A list - an array list, or a `Traversable` read with `foreach` - names one URI per row; one array or object names one URI. An array row is read as it is, an object row as `(array)`, so its public properties. An empty list names none. A list that can be read only once - a `Generator`, or an `Iterator` that is neither an `IteratorAggregate` nor an `ArrayIterator` - is read once and put back in the body as an `ArrayIterator` with every row, under the keys it yielded; when a key repeats, as `yield from` two lists gives, the rows are a list.
- Without `key`, the body itself holds the rows: a body that is a list of rows names one URI per row, and a body that is one array or object names one URI from its keys or public properties.
- With `key`, a variable any row holds is read from the rows alone. One no row holds is read from the body's top level, then from the `onGet()` arguments. Without `key`, every variable is read that way, as `#[Link]` expands its `href`: `$this->body['id'] = 5` with `app://self/article?id={id}` names `?id=5`, and a list of values under an exploded query variable names one URI per element, as in `#[Purge]`: `['id' => [1, 2, 3, 5]]` with `app://self/item{?id*}`, or `['ids' => [1, 2, 3, 5]]` with `app://self/item?id={ids*}`.
- A value that cannot expand - an array, or an object that is not `Stringable`, other than a list of values under an exploded query variable - counts as absent, so the next source is read: `$this->body['user'] = ['id' => $user, 'name' => ...]` with `app://self/item?id={user}` and `onGet(string $user)` expands from the argument.
- A row that lacks a variable is skipped, as a guide row put among article rows; the declaration fails only when no row has it. With `key`, an empty list names no URI. Without `key` and with no row - a `null` body, as a 404 without one has, or an empty list - a template the top level and the arguments fill names its URI, and one they do not names none.
- The arguments are read back from the request query, under the parameter name or its snake_case form, then from the parameter default. A parameter bound by `#[ResourceParam]`, on the parameter or on the method, takes its value from another resource whatever the query holds, so a declaration that uses it fails unless the body holds the value under that name; the resource it is read from is a dependency without a declaration (see Cache Dependencies). A value another provider binds (a web context attribute) is not in the query either: with a default, the URI silently expands from the default instead of the bound value; without one, the declaration fails. A query value is the string the request sent, so an `int` argument expands as written and a `BackedEnum` default fails as not scalar.
- Each URI adds a tag to the `Surrogate-Key` header: 1,000 IDs make it about 24 KB, beyond Fastly's 16,384-byte header limit.
- A declaration on a parent class, or on the `onGet()` a child class overrides, applies as well.
- A `Stringable` value expands as its string. A `null` value names no URI and adds no tag; so does a `null` element of a list.
- A URI also tagged by hand with `UriTagInterface::fromAssoc()` is tagged once.
- `#[DependsOn]` only adds the tag. The URI is invalidated by the named resource's own write, or by a `#[Purge]`/`#[Refresh]` that names it.

A declaration that cannot expand fails the GET with `BEAR\QueryRepository\Exception\DependsOnNotExpandable`, and nothing is stored. Its `reason` is `no '<variable>'` (no such argument), `'<variable>' is not an onGet() parameter` (nor a key of the row or the body), `'<variable>' is bound by #[ResourceParam]` (and not a key of the row or the body) or `'<variable>' is <type>` (neither scalar, `Stringable` nor `null`; a list only under an exploded query variable). Only a declaration on `onGet()` is read; static analysis reports one on a class (PHPStan `attribute.target`, Psalm `InvalidAttribute`).

A row added to a list is caught by the write that adds it, not by the row tags: that write must invalidate the list's own URI, or a URI the list's `onGet()` declares. An embedded list that ran with a body gives the page its own URI tag whether or not it is cached, so a write that invalidates the list's URI reaches the page too.

An embedded child need not be cached for its declarations to reach the page. When the page is stored, the declarations of each embedded child that ran, and of the requests those embed and ran, are read whatever their response code. A request that answered 200 without setting a body cannot be told from one that has not run, so its declarations are not read: an `onGet()` that declares returns `[]` or a 404 when it has no rows; a child rendered later as a hole adds its declarations to the page's `Surrogate-Key`. The declared tags reach the page with the child's own URI tag, through each uncached child between it and the page.

## Modules

### QueryRepositoryModule

Base module: binds the core with a `NullAdapter` store (nothing is kept), a `NullPurger` and the cache log off, and installs the `#[Cacheable]` and donut interceptors. Storage and CDN modules replace its defaults: `$module->override(new StorageRedisDsnModule(...))`.

### StorageRedisDsnModule

Configures Redis-backed storage.

```php
use BEAR\QueryRepository\StorageRedisDsnModule;

new StorageRedisDsnModule('redis://localhost:6379');
// optional: $options, $defaultLifetime, $marshallingOptions (e.g. ['enabled' => true, 'type' => 'deflate'])
```

### StorageMemcachedModule

Configures Memcached-backed storage.

```php
use BEAR\QueryRepository\StorageMemcachedModule;

new StorageMemcachedModule('mem1.example.com:11211:33,mem2.example.com:11211:67'); // {host}:{port}[:{weight}], comma-separated
```

### CDN Modules

```php
use BEAR\QueryRepository\Cdn\AkamaiModule;
use BEAR\QueryRepository\Cdn\FastlyModule;

new FastlyModule($fastlyApiKey, $fastlyServiceId); // requires bear/fastly-module
new AkamaiModule();
```

`FastlyModule` sets `Surrogate-Control` and purges by surrogate key through the Fastly API. `AkamaiModule` only sets the headers (`Akamai-Cache-Control`, `Surrogate-Key` renamed to `Edge-Cache-Tag`); it binds no purger, so a purge does not reach Akamai unless the app binds its own `PurgerInterface`.

### Other modules

- `CacheVersionModule($version)`: the cache namespace. Deploy with a new version so entries stored by the previous one are not read.
- `AppSurrogateKeyModule($key)`: every entry is stored with the key and every `Surrogate-Key` this package sets carries it, so `invalidateTags([$key])` and a CDN purge by the key clear what this package caches. `invalidateTags([$key])` clears the local pool and calls the bound CDN purger; a purge sent to the CDN directly clears only the CDN, which then refills from the local entries. A `Surrogate-Key` a resource sets on a response this package neither stores nor writes as a donut does not get it. Install it before or after `QueryRepositoryModule`.
- `StorageExpiryModule($short, $medium, $long)`: the `short`/`medium`/`long` presets (60/3600/86400 by default); bind `Expiry` to change `never` too.
- `DevEtagModule`: ETags derived from the URI instead of the content, for debugging.
- `DevQueryRepositoryLogModule` / `ProdQueryRepositoryLogModule`: turn the cache log on (see below).

### A stored body must serialize

A `#[Cacheable]` body is checked by serializing it before its own entry is stored or its pre-write cleanup runs; an embedded child has run by then, and a cached child has stored its own entry. A value `serialize()` refuses (a closure, a PDO connection, a DOM node, an object whose `__serialize()` throws) fails the request in every environment with the exception `serialize()` throws, unwrapped, and the log records it as `cache_error{operation: write}` with that exception's class and message. A write fails the same way when the GET that refreshes its entry builds such a body, after the write and the purge of its entry, including any CDN purge, have run. A PHP resource such as a stream is not refused: `serialize()` turns it into `0`, so the check passes and the stored copy loses it (`0`, or `null` with a deprecation notice under igbinary); keep resources out of a cached body. A `#[CacheableResponse]`/`#[DonutCache]` page stores its rendered view, so its body is not checked; under the deprecated `MobileEtagModule` a `#[CacheableResponse]` page's body must serialize too, since its ETag serializes it.

The exception is a page whose renderer encodes the body as JSON: its template is the body it returned (see Donut Caching), so that body, without its embedded requests, is checked the same way when the page is stored. A request nested in an array of that body is refused too, as `serialize()` refuses a request.

### Client Cache-Control of a #[Cacheable] response

A `#[Cacheable]` response is stored with its client `Cache-Control`: `max-age` from `expiryAt`, then `expirySecond`, then the preset, or `max-age=0` when the declaration has no lifetime (the default `expiry: 'never'`, for content that lives until a write invalidates it; data that changes without a write, such as a dashboard or stock prices, declares a lifetime). An `expiryAt` already past resolves to no lifetime (`resolvedTtl: 0`): no `max-age` is added, not even `max-age=0`, and the entry is stored without expiry (`requestedTtl: 0`), so it is served until a write invalidates it. `max-age=0` makes a browser revalidate with the ETag, while an `s-maxage` from `#[HttpCache]` still governs a shared cache. A hit replays the stored directive with `Age`, so a client counts down the same lifetime. A `Cache-Control` that already has `max-age` (from `#[HttpCache]` or the resource) is kept; other directives get the lifetime appended. A response whose own code marked it unstorable (`private` or `no-store`) gets none. A class-level `#[CacheableResponse]` response, which the attribute stores without a lifetime, gets `max-age=0` by the same rule on a 2xx or 3xx, both when stored and when recomposed; one that answers 4xx/5xx or sets its own ETag is not stored (`put_skipped` reason `error-code` / `etag-present`) and gets none. A `#[DonutCache]` page is not affected, nor is an `onGet()` carrying a method-level `#[CacheableResponse]`, which stores only the template the same way.

## Cache Dependencies

A child taken in with `#[Embed]` that ran with a body - a material: the parent's `onGet()` read it, or a `#[Cacheable]` parent ran it, as it runs every top-level embedded request before storing - is a dependency of its parent whether or not it has a cache attribute, an ETag or a `Surrogate-Key`. Its key (its URI tag and its group tag) goes into the parent's stored tags and `Surrogate-Key`, with the tags it carries and those it, or a request it embeds and ran, declares with `#[DependsOn]`: invalidating the child, or a URI it declares, then invalidates the parent. A `#[Cacheable]` parent and a donut page apply the same test. A hole has not run when the page is stored and has no body, so its tags never reach the stored template (see Donut Caching). A value fetched eagerly in `onGet()` (`$this->resource->get(...)`) is not an embedded request and is not tracked.

A resource that `#[ResourceParam]` reads an `onGet()` argument from, declared on the parameter or on the method (the method's when both name the parameter, as BEAR.Resource binds it), is a dependency like an `#[Embed]` child: the resource that read it takes its URI tag and its group tag, and the `Surrogate-Key` of its stored entry when it has one. Its own write invalidates the reader, whether or not the source is cached, as does a `#[Purge]`/`#[Refresh]` or a `purge()` that names it. The URI is the one the argument was read from: a `templated` one is expanded from the request query. A reader that is not cached itself passes these tags to the parent that embeds it, as it passes its `#[DependsOn]` declarations. A source's own `#[DependsOn]` declarations reach the reader only through its stored entry. Cache such a source with `#[Cacheable]`: a `#[CacheableResponse]` or `#[DonutCache]` resource answers a cache hit without its body, so `#[ResourceParam]` cannot read the field from it.

A `#[Cacheable]` resource is stored with what it embeds and what `#[ResourceParam]` reads, as they were at that moment; a class-level `#[CacheableResponse]` page is stored the same way, together with what its holes rendered. Each serves that until a dependency is invalidated or the entry expires. The template of a `#[DonutCache]` page is kept likewise; only its holes run on every request. Keep what differs per user, such as the session, out of what is stored: one user's result would be served to every other. A per-user child belongs in a hole of a `#[DonutCache]` page.

A stored value can be built again at any time: after a deploy, an eviction or its expiry, it is made from what its sources hold then. A value that must be kept, such as the day's highest temperature, is saved by a write, not left to the cache.

```php
#[Cacheable]
class BlogPost extends ResourceObject
{
    #[Embed(rel: 'comments', src: 'app://self/comments{?id}')]
    public function onGet(int $id): static
    {
        $this->body['post'] = $this->getPost($id);
        return $this;
    }
}
```

Whether or not `app://self/comments` is itself cached, a write to `app://self/comments?id=…` invalidates the BlogPost entry through its surrogate keys. A write whose query lacks a parameter the comments' `onGet()` requires addresses no entry and is logged as `purge_skipped`.

On a `#[CacheableResponse]`/`#[DonutCache]` page the same rule applies to a child whose value `onGet()` reads: the whole template is dropped on purge. A child the page only renders as a hole is recomposed instead. A hole whose class declares a default `$body` has a body before it runs, so it is taken as a material: its URI tag reaches the template, and a purge of it rebuilds the page.

A child a cached parent embeds takes one of two shapes:

- **A material**: the child ran with a body before the parent was stored - the parent's `onGet()` read it, or a `#[Cacheable]` parent ran it. Its key, with the tags it carries, goes into the parent's stored tags, cached or not, so a change to it invalidates the parent. A non-cached child in between passes the keys and tags of the children below it on with its own, so a change below it reaches the parent too.
- **A hole**: on a `#[CacheableResponse]`/`#[DonutCache]` page, a child the page only renders. It is never part of the stored template. On a `#[DonutCache]` page it runs on every request, so per-user or per-request values belong there; a class-level `#[CacheableResponse]` page stores what the hole rendered until the hole is purged.

Caching the parent caches a material too, even though the child declares no cache: the parent serves the child's data as it was stored until the child's key, or a tag it carries, is invalidated, or the parent's TTL expires. A top-level child with no body when the parent is stored is not a material. It is still a dependency when it carries an ETag, a `Surrogate-Key` or a `#[DependsOn]` declaration; otherwise the log records it as `dependency_skipped` (reason `no_body`), on a donut page usually a hole.

A list of rows read directly - not embedded one by one - ties itself to each row's URI the same way: `#[DependsOn]` under Attributes above tags the list's own `Surrogate-Key`, without an `#[Embed]` for each row.

Dependencies and holes are found where `#[Embed]` puts a child: at the top level of the body. A request the page moves into a nested array, replaces or `unset()`s before the write is not seen. On a `#[CacheableResponse]`/`#[DonutCache]` page a nested request does not become a hole either: when the template prints it, it runs and its output is written into the stored template, its tags reach no one, and nothing is logged. The page then shows that child's old content until the page's own TTL, and a per-user child nested this way puts one visitor's content into the template every visitor shares.

A child the template fetches while rendering, from a template helper for example, is written into the stored template the same way. A dependency the template declares while rendering, with `CacheDependencyInterface::depends()` for example, is not supported: it may still log `depends_on` and reach the response's `Surrogate-Key`, but not the stored template, so purging the child recomposes the page's old content. Embed such a child at the top level of the page body instead, with `#[Embed]` or an interceptor that puts the request there as `#[Embed]` does. A per-user child still does not belong in the template.

A list whose length, order or queries come from data (blocks an editor arranges, say) cannot be written as `#[Embed]` on the page, which is static. Build it in a child resource instead, embed that child, and let the child list the block requests at the top level of its own body - the child's write is read the same way:

```php
// The page embeds the composed list and prints it whole: (string) $this->contents
#[CacheableResponse]
class Channel extends ResourceObject
{
    #[Embed(rel: 'contents', src: 'app://self/channel/blocks{?slug}')]
    public function onGet(string $slug): static
    {
        return $this;
    }
}
```

```php
// app://self/channel/blocks
#[Cacheable]
class Blocks extends ResourceObject
{
    #[Embed(rel: 'whatsNew', src: 'app://self/block/whats-new')]
    #[Embed(rel: 'feature', src: 'app://self/block/feature')]
    public function onGet(string $slug): static
    {
        // requests at the top level, order in plain data; the prototypes are not kept
        $this->body = [
            'layout' => [['key' => 'whats_new_0', 'type' => 'whatsNew'], ['key' => 'feature_1', 'type' => 'feature']],
            'whats_new_0' => (clone $this['whatsNew'])->withQuery(['slug' => $slug, 'limit' => 5]),
            'feature_1' => (clone $this['feature'])->withQuery(['slug' => $slug, 'limit' => 3]),
        ];

        return $this;
    }
}
```

Make the composing child `#[Cacheable]`; the blocks are its materials, so their keys reach it whether or not they are cached. All of them are shared by every visitor, so a per-user block stays out of the list and becomes a hole on a `#[DonutCache]` page. Clones of one prototype share a single resource object, so on a donut child running one clone makes its unrun siblings look run; a `#[Cacheable]` child runs each top-level request right before reading its keys.

On a donut page a top-level embedded request becomes a hole that can only be printed, not iterated: print the child whole and iterate `layout` in the child's own template.

## Donut Caching

A page stores its rendered template; each child it takes in with `#[Embed]` and only renders is a hole. A `#[DonutCache]` page runs its holes and renders them into the template on every request. A class-level `#[CacheableResponse]` page also stores the page as its holes rendered it, and answers with that stored page without running them. A value fetched in `onGet()` with `$this->resource->get()` is part of the template, not a hole.

```php
use BEAR\RepositoryModule\Annotation\DonutCache;
use BEAR\Resource\Annotation\Embed;

#[DonutCache]
class BlogPage extends ResourceObject
{
    #[Embed(rel: 'comment', src: 'app://self/comment')] // hole
    public function onGet(): static
    {
        $this->body['article'] = '1'; // template
        return $this;
    }
}
```

- `#[DonutCache]`: stores the template only; holes run on every request. For per-user holes.
- `#[CacheableResponse]`: also stores the composed page; a hole's purge recomposes it from the template. A write method of the class purges and rebuilds the page.
- `#[CacheableResponse]` on `onGet()` alone stores the template only, as `#[DonutCache]` does. A write method marked `#[RefreshCache]` purges and rebuilds its own URI.
- Under a renderer that encodes the body as JSON, such as the JSON and HAL renderers, the template is the body the page returned, with each embedded request left out: a template hit renders that body again with those requests put back, and does not run `onGet()`. The page shows what it shows without the attribute.

## Cache Log (Semantic Log)

The reader's guide to this vocabulary is `docs/reading-the-log.md`; the tables below are the lookup form of the same facts.

Cache operations are logged as an open/event/close tree (Koriym.SemanticLogger) whose nesting **is** the embed/dependency structure: a parent's embedded child GETs appear as nested scopes, no reconstruction needed. Every entry carries a typed context object and a `schemaUrl` pointing at its per-context JSON Schema, so the log is self-describing.

### Log Contexts

| Context (type) | Kind | Description |
|----------------|------|-------------|
| `get` | open | A resource/donut GET scope; embedded child GETs nest under it |
| `cache_hit` / `cache_miss` (`layer`) | close/event | Lookup outcome (`layer`: `resource` / `donut` / `donut-view` / `etag`) |
| `command` (`method`/`annotations`/`source`) | open | A write scope; `source` names the producing interceptor, `annotations` its `#[Refresh]`/`#[Purge]` attributes (empty on the CacheableResponse path by design) |
| `depends_on` (`parent`/`child`/`childTags`) | event | Parent registered a dependency on a child. A `#[Cacheable]` parent records it on put for each top-level child that ran with a body, cached or not (the child's URI tag and group tag, with the tags it carries, land on `save_value`/`save_view`); a donut page write records it for each material — a child whose `onGet()` reads it — whose tags land on `save_donut` too. A hole records `dependency_skipped` instead: its tags reach `save_donut_view` (`#[CacheableResponse]`) or only `cdn_headers.surrogateKeys` (`#[DonutCache]`), never `save_donut`. A child that ran and declares `#[DependsOn]`, itself or in a request it embeds and ran, records one whatever its code, so its own URI tag reaches the parent; each declared tag lands in `childTags` here and in the parent's `save_*` `tags` too. When the resource being stored reads an `onGet()` argument with `#[ResourceParam]`, it records one with the resource it read from as the `child`; a reader embedded without a cache of its own records none, and that resource's tags appear in the reader's `childTags` instead |
| `dependency_skipped` (`parent`/`child`/`reason`) | event | A cached parent's write (a `#[Cacheable]` put or a donut page write) left a top-level embedded child out of its dependencies: the child had no body. A child that has a body is a dependency, tagged or not. `reason` is what its body showed: `no_body` (null; on a donut page usually a hole). `no_etag_or_surrogate_key`, which 1.20.2 recorded for a child with neither header, stays in the schema and is no longer emitted. `docs/reading-the-log.md` explains it |
| `save_value` / `save_view` / `save_donut` / `save_donut_view` | event | What was offered to the pool, with `tags`, `requestedTtl` (seconds until expiry; 0/null = no expiry set), and the `saved` outcome: `true` = the pool accepted it, not that it is kept — `NullAdapter`, the store when none is bound, accepts every write and keeps nothing |
| `pre_write_cleanup` (`uri`) | event | Marker recorded by a writer right before it clears a stored entry it found where it writes; a write into an empty slot records none. The `invalidate` immediately following it in the same scope is pre-write cleanup, not a real invalidation |
| `invalidate` (`tags`/`roPool`/`cdn`/`durationMs`) | event | Tag invalidation outcome; `cdn` is tri-state: `purged` (a configured purger ran), `failed` (the purge threw — fail-closed, after the local pool was invalidated), `skipped` (NullPurger, no CDN configured). Pre-write cleanup vs real invalidation is recorded at the source via the `pre_write_cleanup` marker — see below |
| `cdn_headers` (`uri`/`headers`/`surrogateKeys`) | event | The CDN-facing headers a donut write or refresh put on the response, read back after they are final: the literal name => value pairs (`CDN-Cache-Control`, `Surrogate-Control`, `Akamai-Cache-Control`, `Surrogate-Key`, `Edge-Cache-Tag`) — including the bound setter's default when no `sMaxAge` was requested. No lifetime header means the response gave the CDN no lifetime directive (the `putDonut` kind); what the CDN then does is outside this log. `surrogateKeys` is the split key list a purge's tags must reach to drop the response at the edge. A state-served hit replays the stored headers and emits no new event |
| `conditional_request` (`ifNoneMatch`) | open | A conditional request presented a validator at the transfer boundary; closes `cache_hit`/`cache_miss` at layer `etag`: a hit when the stored entry the validator names carries it. A hit is the 304 decision — the entire request answered without running the resource, which no `get` scope can show. No `If-None-Match` presents nothing and records nothing. Flushing stays the host's responsibility: flush before an early-exit 304 transfer to retain it |
| `purge` | event | An explicit purge request |
| `purge_skipped` (`uri`/`reason`) | event | A write on a resource with neither `#[Cacheable]` nor `#[CacheableResponse]` did not invalidate its own key (`reason`: `unmatched_query`, its query lacks a parameter its `onGet()` requires, as a creating POST has no id yet). `uri` is the write's URI without its query, which holds the values the write was sent. Its `#[Purge]`/`#[Refresh]` still run |
| `put_skipped` (`uri`/`reason`[/`code`]) | event | A miss was not followed by a put (`reason`: `etag-present` / `error-code` with the actual response `code` / `not-cacheable` / `unstorable`) |
| `cache_error` (`uri`/`operation`/`error`/`exceptionClass`) | event | A failure raised on the cache read/write path: the pool itself (e.g. cache server down) or any work the store performs (rendering a view, purging a CDN); `operation`: `read` / `write`, `exceptionClass` names the throwable that failed |
| `put_donut` / `refresh_donut` | event | Donut store / re-render from a template hit |
| `semantic_logger_error` (`code` + details) | event | Core SemanticLogger diagnostic (koriym/semantic-logger, not this package): logging-protocol misuse recorded in-band at the exact failure point — codes: `close_id_mismatch` / `close_without_open` / `unclosed_at_flush` / `context_serialization_failed`; the tree is preserved |
| `manual_store` / `manual_purge` / `manual_invalidate` (+ `*_result` closes) | open | Scope rooting a top-level (non-AOP) call: `put()` / `putStatic()` / `putDonut()` (`manual_store`), `purge()` (`manual_purge`), `invalidateTags()` (`manual_invalidate`). A donut write's own pre-write cleanup invalidation nests inside its `manual_store` instead of rooting a `manual_invalidate` of its own. In a `manual_invalidate` scope the `invalidate` detail stays a nested event — so tag correlation finds manual invalidations too — and the close is the one-word verdict (`manual_invalidate_result`) |

A donut refresh is not marked in any response header — only in the log (`refresh_donut`). The ETag stays a pure validator of the representation: it changes when the recomposed content changed, and a recomposition yielding identical content keeps its entity-tag and still answers `If-None-Match` with 304.

### Turning the log on, and where a session goes

- Off by default (`QueryRepositoryModule`): `SemanticLoggerInterface` annotated with `#[CacheLog]` → `Koriym\SemanticLogger\NullSemanticLogger`. The qualifier is why installing this package cannot decide an application's own `SemanticLoggerInterface` binding; resolve the cache log with `getInstance(SemanticLoggerInterface::class, CacheLog::class)`. Nothing is recorded, nothing accumulates, no flush is owed — the same rule the package already applies to its cache engine (`NullAdapter`). A measured healthy read carries no information (0 failure entries out of 28-95 per session in the four demos), while a recorded session costs ~1.4 KB per request until something flushes it, so recording is something an app asks for.
- Development: `new DevQueryRepositoryLogModule($appDir . '/var/log/query-repository', module: new QueryRepositoryModule())`. Every session is written whole, one file per process — one request under PHP-FPM, every request of a CLI script that makes several — plus a fixed `latest.json` — `vendor/bin/stree var/log/query-repository/latest.json` renders the session that just ran. Note the wrapping: a module's `install()` cannot replace a binding the installer already holds (`Container::merge()` keeps existing keys), which is why the log module takes the module it turns recording on for, exactly as `DevEtagModule` does.
- Production: `new ProdQueryRepositoryLogModule('php://stdout', sampleRate: 1000, module: new QueryRepositoryModule())`. The session is buffered and judged at flush (`RetentionPolicyInterface`), and the line is who else knows rather than success-vs-failure: mutations (a `command` scope, a `manual_*` call, or an `invalidate` that is not marker-preceded pre-write cleanup), effects that were intended and did not happen (`saved: false`, `invalidate` with `roPool`/`cdn` `failed`, a `manual_*` result of `failed`, `cache_error{operation: write}` - a store or an invalidation abandoned), and an optional sample. Healthy reads are dropped, and so is one thing that looks like an incident but is accounted for elsewhere: `cache_error{operation: read}` is already reported by the application's own warning channel - both interceptors `trigger_error()` before degrading, for every cause and not only the outage a pool's monitoring would see - and it repeats on every request while the incident lasts (so the separation of a degraded miss from a cold one is a development-time reading). Every `put_skipped` records a store that was never attempted because a rule forbade it - a response code the path will not cache (`#[Cacheable]` skips any non-200, a donut skips 4xx and above), a validator already set, or a page served from its template - which is a decision, stable while the code and the configuration are, rather than a runtime failure, so none of its reasons keep a session on their own. A body a stored entry cannot hold (`serialize()` refusing a closure, say) fails the request instead of producing a skip, and `cache_error{operation: write}` - already one of the kept effects above - records the refusal. Retention keeps or drops whole sessions: the dropped events do not keep a session on their own, and a session kept for another reason still carries them. `saved: false` can still repeat per write under a capacity problem: that is the signal, and a host that needs a ceiling decorates `LogWriterInterface`. This buys forensics, not monitoring — hit rates belong to metrics. An app that wants full recording for one request implements `RetentionPolicyInterface` and overrides the binding, since only the app knows what authorizes it.
- A written session is application-log material, not an artefact: it records resource URIs **with their query strings** (`AbstractUri::__toString()` appends them, so `page://self/reset?token=…` is written in full; the URI of a write that cannot address its own key, in `purge_skipped` or `cache_error`, is recorded without its query, which holds the values the write was sent), the client's raw `If-None-Match`, `$_SERVER['REQUEST_URI']` on the `HttpCache` path, cache/surrogate tags, CDN header values, and `cache_error.error` - the verbatim `getMessage()` of whatever the read/write path threw, which for an HTTP CDN purger can carry the purge endpoint and its credentials. No response body is recorded by any context. `LogFileWriter` therefore creates its directory 0700 and its files 0600, and a host that must scrub decorates `LogWriterInterface` rather than waiting for a redaction option: the seam is one class (`final class Scrubbed implements LogWriterInterface { public function __construct(private LogWriterInterface $inner) {} }`). The same seam rate-limits: during a cache-pool outage every request emits `cache_error`, so retention rises from `1/sampleRate` to 100% - a decorator that caps kept sessions per interval keeps an incident from flooding the collector it exists to inform.
- Destinations are `LogWriterInterface` implementations, so a session's payload stays a tree rather than a string: `LogFileWriter` (one whole session per file — what `stree` reads), `LogStreamWriter` (one JSON line per session to a stream or file), `PolicyLogWriter` (the retention decorator) and `PsrLogWriter`, which hands the tree to the app's PSR-3 logger under the `log` context key. PSR-3 is an adapter and not the interface for two reasons: it carries strings, so a `LineFormatter` would flatten the tree the schemas describe, and its severity would act as a second filter able to drop what the content-based retention policy chose to keep (the level is configuration on the adapter, never derived).
- One flush, several destinations: the log modules declare an empty `LogWriterInterface` set, and the sink passes each flushed session to the bound writer and then to every writer added with `MultiBinder::newInstance($this, LogWriterInterface::class)->addBinding()->to(X::class)`, in the order added. Adding replaces no binding, so install order cannot drop a destination; decorating stays the way to change what the bound writer gets. An added writer gets every session unfiltered: `PolicyLogWriter` retention and any decorator apply to the bound writer only, so an added writer scrubs and samples for itself. A writer that throws is reported to `error_log()` and the rest still run. Bind `X` as well (`$this->bind(X::class)`): a compiled injector builds only bound classes, so an unbound one works under `Ray\Di\Injector` and fails in production (ray-di/Ray.Compiler#148).
- Both log modules bind `SemanticLoggerInterface` annotated with `#[CacheLog]` → `SafeSemanticLogger` in singleton scope via `SafeSemanticLoggerProvider`, with the session of the request in progress resolved through `SessionStoreInterface` (`ProcessSession`, one per process, by default). The core logger never throws (koriym/semantic-logger 0.9), so a logging failure cannot break a cache read/write; `SafeSemanticLogger` keeps open-scope depth on the `Session` the store resolves and keeps no session across the serialization boundary.
- Manual-scope rooting (`manual_store` / `manual_purge` / `manual_invalidate`) is granted by the `TopLevelAwareInterface` capability (`isTopLevel()`), which `SafeSemanticLogger` implements; a custom `SemanticLoggerInterface` decorator can implement it to mark top-level direct calls as application-initiated in its sessions. Without it those calls are recorded as bare root-level events.
- Flushing is owned by the log module, not the app: it binds `LogSinkInterface` → `ShutdownFlush`, which registers the flush once per process at construction and again at `SafeSemanticLogger::__unserialize()` — the only hook that runs on every request, since a module's `configure()` runs once at compile time. A shutdown-time flush is deliberate: rendering happens inside `ResourceObject::transfer()`, so cache reads are still recorded while the response is written, and a 304 answer never reaches that method at all (`HttpCacheInterface::transfer()` sets the status and the caller stops, typically with `exit`). Shutdown functions run after output, after `exit()` and after an uncaught error. `flush()` never throws and always resets, so it needs no guard, and an empty session is never written. `ShutdownFlush` refuses to arm and warns on a runtime it can prove is concurrent (`RR_MODE` set, or inside a Swoole coroutine): there shutdown arrives once per worker and concurrent requests share one session — bind a request-scoped `LogSinkInterface`, or leave the log module out, until coroutine-local scoping lands (#179). Interleaved sessions surface as `semantic_logger_error` diagnostics rather than silently.

### Verifying the event-driven cache from logs

- Event-driven entries appear with their configured TTL in seconds (`requestedTtl` = seconds until expiry; the `never` convention = 31536000 = 1 year, effectively indefinite — the TTL asked of the store, not a browser lifetime: a declaration without a lifetime, a lifetime-less `#[Cacheable]` or a class-level `#[CacheableResponse]`, sends the client `max-age=0`). `0`/`null` also mean no expiry is set. Such entries live until an `invalidate` event with a matching tag — correlate `save_*` `tags` with `invalidate` `tags` to confirm a write busted its dependents. Which `save_*` carries a child's tags is decided by the parent's declaration: `#[Cacheable]` puts them on `save_value`/`save_view`, records a `depends_on` edge as well, and the parent closes `cache_miss` once the child is purged; a donut parent separates two uses: a data dependency (a child `onGet()` read) records `depends_on` and tags the template and the view, so purging it makes the next read a `cache_miss`; a hole (run by the template, not before the write) records `dependency_skipped` instead of an edge and tags the view only, so purging it still closes `cache_hit{layer: donut-view}` with a `refresh_donut` inside — a hit with no `refresh_donut` is the stale shape. A part the page renders is embedded at the top level of the page body, with `#[Embed]` or an interceptor that puts the request there as `#[Embed]` does; a dependency the template declares while rendering, with `CacheDependencyInterface::depends()` for example, is not supported (the tell: a `depends_on` whose `childTags` are missing from `save_donut`), and a child inlined by other means is not tracked at all. A `#[DonutCache]` page stores no view, so its holes' tags reach only `cdn_headers.surrogateKeys`, and every read after the first is `refresh_donut` + `put_skipped{not-cacheable}`.
- A `get` scope with no events and a `cache_hit` close was served from cache; nesting mirrors the embed structure of resources; `manual_*` scopes mark non-AOP entry points — a direct `put()`, `purge()`, `invalidateTags()` or donut write (`putStatic()`/`putDonut()`), the whole write rooted in one `manual_store` scope.
- A miss scope without `save_*` events means nothing was stored — look for a `put_skipped` event recording why (`reason`: `etag-present`, `error-code` with the actual response `code`, `not-cacheable` for donut pages served from their template plus inner caches, or `unstorable` for a response marked unstorable for this request or carrying a `private`/`no-store` `Cache-Control`), or a `cache_error{operation: write}` when the put failed: a body `serialize()` refuses fails the request this way, with no `put_skipped`. A non-200 GET yields `put_skipped{error-code, code}` + `purge` + `invalidate` (for commands, a 4xx `command_result` with no invalidation events).
- An `invalidate` is pre-write cleanup iff the event immediately preceding it in the same scope's event stream is a `pre_write_cleanup` marker — the writer records the purpose at the source (`QueryRepository::doPut()` and `DonutRepository::putStatic()`/`putDonut()` emit the marker right before clearing a stored entry they found where they write), so nothing is inferred from tag correlation and no case is undecidable. A write into an empty slot - the write after a miss - clears nothing and records neither, so the other variants of the URI and the parents that embed it stay stored. Any `invalidate` without the marker is a real invalidation (a `#[Refresh]` command shows that shape alone: its purge empties the slot, so the GET that rebuilds the entry records no marker). The cleanup uses the entry's URI tag — which is also its parents' surrogate key — so a write that replaces an entry drops the parents that embed it, by design.
- Check outcome fields: `saved: false` on a save context means the pool rejected the entry — it is NOT cached despite the save event. `cdn` on `invalidate` is tri-state: `purged` (a configured purger ran), `failed` (the purge threw; fail-closed, after the local pool was invalidated), `skipped` (NullPurger, no CDN configured). A `cache_error` event records a failure on the cache path, not necessarily a cache outage: read `exceptionClass` before concluding one, because `operation: write` also covers the work the store performs (a view that fails to render, a CDN purge that throws). A pool exception on `operation: read` means the store could not be read, so the `cache_miss` after it reports a failed lookup rather than an absent entry. `semantic_logger_error` events are core SemanticLogger diagnostics (codes: `close_id_mismatch`, `close_without_open`, `unclosed_at_flush`, `context_serialization_failed`) recording logging-protocol misuse in-band at the exact failure point — the log tree itself is preserved.
- Events and nested scopes within one scope are interleaved in one `log` list, in record order (resolved upstream: koriym/semantic-logger's `log` format replaces the old separate `open`/`events` arrays). Use that order, plus scope nesting and the next GET's hit/miss, as ground truth for final state after competing save/invalidate.

Schemas: docs/schemas/context/ (one JSON Schema per context, e.g. docs/schemas/context/save_value.json; each log entry links its own via `schemaUrl`)

## Architecture

### Core Components

- **QueryRepository**: Main entry point for cache operations (put, get, purge)
- **ResourceStorage**: Low-level storage using Symfony Cache TagAwareAdapter: one resource pool, whose entries carry the ETag a conditional request is checked against
- **CacheInterceptor**: AOP interceptor on `onGet()` of #[Cacheable] resources
- **CommandInterceptor**: On write methods of #[Cacheable] resources: runs `RefreshSameCommand` (purge and re-GET its own URI) and `RefreshAnnotatedCommand` (#[Refresh]/#[Purge])
- **RefreshInterceptor**: #[Refresh]/#[Purge] on a resource that is not #[Cacheable]
- **DonutRepository**: Implements donut caching pattern (`DonutCacheInterceptor`, `DonutCacheableResponseInterceptor` on reads, `DonutCommandInterceptor` on writes)
- **CacheDependency**: Manages cache dependencies via Surrogate-Key headers

### Cache Invalidation Flow

1. A write method runs; the interceptor acts only when it answers below 400
2. The resource's own URI, default-valued `onGet()` parameters dropped, is purged and rebuilt by a GET on a new resource instance (`RefreshSameCommand` for #[Cacheable], `DonutCommandInterceptor` for #[CacheableResponse] or #[RefreshCache])
3. Each #[Purge] URI is purged; each #[Refresh] URI is purged and rebuilt by a GET
4. A purge invalidates the URI's tag and its group tag: ResourceStorage::invalidateTags() clears the pool, then the `PurgerInterface` (CDN) runs; a failing CDN purge throws after the local pool is cleared

## Documentation

- Manual: https://bearsunday.github.io/manuals/1.0/en/cache.html
- Repository: https://github.com/bearsunday/BEAR.QueryRepository

## Schemas

- Cache log context schemas: https://bearsunday.github.io/BEAR.QueryRepository/schemas/context/ (one JSON Schema per context, e.g. https://bearsunday.github.io/BEAR.QueryRepository/schemas/context/save_value.json)
